# Fundamental Physics

Our current understanding of physics is governed by two theories, general relativity and the Standard Model of particle physics (the latter a quantum field theory).

Both theories have successfully passed extensive experimental testing. Conservatively, general relativity is well confirmed for classical gravity across field strengths from the Solar System to black holes, and its Newtonian limit holds down to about 50 micrometres. Likewise, the Standard Model reliably describes a wide range of experimentally tested electromagnetic, weak, and strong interactions, from atomic energy scales ($\sim 1$ eV) to selected high-energy processes at approximately 1-3 TeV ($10^{12}$-$3 \times 10^{12}$ eV), probing distance scales of order $10^{-19}$ metres, with predictions generally agreeing with measurements within experimental and theoretical uncertainties.

At everyday scales, complex physics mathematically simplifies into familiar rules. General relativity reduces to Newton's laws because we move slowly and Earth's gravity is relatively weak. Nuclear forces stay locked completely inside atomic nuclei. Quantum electrodynamics (the quantum version of electromagnetism) scales up into everyday forces like friction, light, and chemical bonds.

Exploring these theories and their building blocks, this website contains some of the most familiar results with the least mathematical prerequisites I found while reading "The Theoretical Minimum" book series by Susskind and co-authors, "The Biggest Ideas in the Universe" book series by Sean M Carroll, and other sources of a similar spirit/difficulty level.
